# {0}Minecraft Console Client
A Minecraft client that runs in your terminal. Type to chat, run `/commands`, and automate things with plugins.
Shorter version of the Help page: `Mcc.Cli --help-short`
> [!NOTE] > Never used a terminal program before? You only need one line to start. Everything else is optional.
## {1}New here? Start here
1. Run `Mcc.Cli` with no arguments. 2. MCC creates a `configurations/` folder with commented examples on the first run. 3. It asks how you want to sign in, then connects you.
That is it. Come back to this page later when you want shortcuts.
## {2}How to run it
```text Mcc.Cli [<username>] [<password|->] [<host[:port]>] [--configurations <folder>] [-v <version>] [--auth <mode>] [--auth-server <host>] [--exercise <name>] [--section.setting=value ...] ```
The words after `Mcc.Cli` are called **arguments**. Order matters: the first word is always the username, the second the password, the third the server address. Anything in `[brackets]` is optional, so `Mcc.Cli` alone is valid. To reach a later slot, fill the earlier ones: use `-` for the password when you have nothing for it.
## {3}The 3 arguments, in order
| # | What to type | What it does | Example | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | `username` | Who to sign in as. Offline names hold 16 chars max. | `Steve` | | 2 | `password` or `-` | `-` forces offline mode. Anything else is accepted but unused, because online sign-in is interactive. | `-` | | 3 | `host[:port]` | Which server to join. The port defaults to `25565`. | `play.example.com:25565` |
Your settings live in `./configurations` unless you pass `--configurations <folder>` (a folder, or a `client.toml` file inside one).
> [!TIP] > The shortest full command names all three: `Mcc.Cli Steve - play.example.com`.
## {4}Options you can add
| Option | What it does | | --- | --- | | `--configurations <folder>` | Use another settings folder instead of `./configurations`. | | `-v <version>` | Pin a Minecraft version, like `1.21.5`. Leave it out for auto-detect. | | `--auth <mode>` | How to sign in. See the signing-in section below. | | `--auth-server <host>` | Custom login server URL. Only used with `--auth yggdrasil`. | | `--exercise <name>` | Run a self-check after joining, then quit. Known value: `smoke`. | | `--section.setting=value` | Change one `client.toml` setting for this run only. Wins over everything else. | | `--console.table.key=value` | Change one `console.toml` setting, for example `--console.General.Timestamps=true`. |
Short flags (`-v`) and long flags (`--auth`) are the same idea: extra instructions that start with dashes so MCC knows they are not usernames or addresses.
## {5}Signing in, explained
| Mode | Pick it when | What happens | | --- | --- | --- | | `offline` | You play on a test or offline-mode server. | No password. Just joins. | | `microsoft` | You have a normal Microsoft account. | Shows a short code and a Microsoft link. Open the link, enter the code. | | `microsoft-browser` | The code flow does not work for you. | Shows a link. Sign in in your browser, then paste back the code it shows. | | `yggdrasil` | Your server uses its own login (authlib-injector). | Asks for a username and password, and needs `--auth-server`. |
Passwords are never saved to disk. Microsoft uses a browser step, Yggdrasil asks each time.
## {6}Tweaking settings without editing files
Your settings live in `client.toml` and `console.toml`. Flags let you try a change once:
```text Mcc.Cli --connection.auto-connect=false Mcc.Cli --gameplay.terrain=false Steve - play.example.com Mcc.Cli --console.General.Timestamps=true ```
The rule is simple: config file < arguments < `--dotted.flags`. The rightmost flag wins.
## {7}Examples you can copy
```text Mcc.Cli Mcc.Cli Steve - play.example.com Mcc.Cli --configurations ./my-config Steve - play.example.com:25565 Mcc.Cli --auth microsoft Steve - play.example.com Mcc.Cli -v 1.21.5 Steve - play.example.com Mcc.Cli --exercise smoke Steve - play.example.com ```
## {8}When you are inside
- Type chat and press Enter to talk, or type `/help` to list commands. - Type `quit` or `exit` to disconnect. - For scripts: set `MCC_FILE_INPUT=1` and point `MCC_INPUT_FILE` at a file of commands.
## {9}Need more help?
- Inside MCC, `/help <command>` and `/man <topic>` explain the rest.
